title: Multi-Cloud Backup Recovery Testing

controlTest.positiveScenario: Inject sample events matching UC-4.4.29 SPL; confirm the search returns rows and alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign traffic without matching markers; confirm UC-4.4.29 search returns zero rows.

dataSources: `index=aws` sourcetype=`aws:cloudwatch:events` collected via `Splunk_TA_aws`, Azure Backup logs, GCP Backup for GKE / Database exports; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
app: `Splunk_TA_aws`, Azure Backup logs, GCP Backup for GKE / Database exports
spl:
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudwatch:events" (  detail-type="Restore Job State Change")
| table _time detail-type source detail.eventName

| sort -_time
description: Untested restores fail when needed; tracking drill outcomes across AWS Backup, Azure Backup, and GCP proves RPO/RTO.
value: Detecting multi-cloud backup recovery testing early reduces mean time to contain cloud incidents, supports audit logging controls, and prevents silent misconfiguration drift across accounts.
implementation: Tag restore jobs with `drill=true` in application metadata. Quarterly dashboard of success rate and restore duration percentiles. Alert on any failed table-top restore.
visualization: Table (app, provider, success/fail), Bar chart (drill outcomes by quarter), Line chart (restore duration trend).
knownFalsePositives: This pattern can surge during change windows, in sandboxes, and when a platform is in maintenance, so we line alerts up with the calendar and take a second look before we call it an incident.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=aws`.
• Install and configure `Splunk_TA_aws`, Azure Backup logs, GCP Backup for GKE / Database exports with the modular input for `aws:cloudwatch:events`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.4.33.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `detail-type` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Tag restore jobs with `drill=true` in application metadata. Quarterly dashboard of success rate and restore duration percentiles. Alert on any failed table-top restore.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudwatch:events" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudwatch:events" (  detail-type="Restore Job State Change")
| table _time detail-type source detail.eventName
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.4.29_multi_cloud_backup_recov_29"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `aws:cloudwatch:events` in `index=aws` to detect multi-cloud backup recovery testing. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the provider cloud console audit view for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `detail-type` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_4_29_alert` with severity aligned to `high` criticality. Dashboard: Table (app, provider, success/fail), Bar chart (drill outcomes by quarter), Line chart (restore duration trend)..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade `Splunk_TA_aws`, Azure Backup logs, GCP Backup for GKE / Database exports and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of multi-cloud backup recovery testing so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
